messages:
eve: Heads up — found a staging S3 snapshot with a file that looks like vault-wrapped key metadata and a leaked GH token. Not public, but within a backup we pulled for debug. :rotating_light:
sec-oncall: Assigned incident. Can you paste the exact filename + bucket? Any PII? :eyes:
eve: s3://redwood-staging-backups/2026-03-08/db_snapshot.tar.gz -> inside: config/vault/wrapped_keys.json and creds/ci-token.txt (short-lived GH PAT used by old job). No PII. Token appears scoped to repo redwood/devops.
alice: Thanks. First priorities: 1) revoke the exposed token, 2) rotate any Vault-transit keys used to wrap secrets referenced in that backup, 3) audit who accessed the backup. I'll take token revoke.
bob: I'm on rewrap/rotation. Which KMS? It looks like the wrapped metadata references KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789. Are we on a rewrap path or create new key+rekey?
carol: Also need to confirm whether Vault used KMS for auto-unseal or as transit-wrapping. From the file contents it looks like transit-wrapped blobs + envelope encryption by AWS KMS for the master key.
dinesh: I'll pull S3 access logs and check IAM principals. Will need timeframe. eve, when did you pull the snapshot?
eve: Pulled yesterday 2026-03-09 14:05 UTC. Snapshot retention policy was 90 days; shouldn't have been exposed but was in a locked bucket with old ACL change in 2025.
sec-oncall: Action list: revoke token (alice) — done?; block access to snapshot (infra-bot will quarantine); generate new KMS CMK and schedule rewrap; rotate vault transit keys; post a short timeline for auditors.
alice: Revoked CI token at 1766002000 (just now). Logged in GH: token revoked 1766001998. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: quarantine: s3://redwood-staging-backups/2026-03-08/db_snapshot.tar.gz => moved to s3://quarantine/redwood-incidents/1766001234/ (actor: infra-bot) [cmd: aws s3 mv s3://redwood-staging-backups/2026-03-08/db_snapshot.tar.gz s3://quarantine/redwood-incidents/1766001234/] :lock:
bob: For rewrap plan: we should create a fresh KMS key (CMK) with tight key policy, add a key alias alias/incidents/rewrap-1766001234, then instruct Vault to rewrap using transit: rekey or rewrap CLI. Proposed steps:
  1) create CMK in us-west-2 w/ admins: kms-admins, deny external account access
  2) create key alias
  3) export list of transit key IDs from wrapped_keys.json
  4) for each key: vault write transit/rewrap ... (or use vault operator rewrap)
Include sample command:
```
# create alias
aws kms create-key --description "Incident rewrap 1766001234" --key-usage ENCRYPT_DECRYPT
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/incidents/rewrap-1766001234 --target-key-id <new-key-id>
# vault rewrap (pseudocode)
vault write transit/rewrap key=<old> rewrap_to_key=<new_kms_key_arn>
```
carol: Note: Vault's rewrap vendor-specific — if using Envelope + KMS, we need to run 'vault rekey' or rewrap; check Vault version. We might need to re-encrypt data using vault operator step.
dinesh: IAM changes: after new CMK is created, rotate policies so only vault-unseal and sec-team can use it. I'll prepare a terraform plan: kms_key.tf with minimal principals. Will push to branch incident/kms-rewrap.
sec-oncall: For compliance timeline, capture: discovery, token revoke time, quarantine time, rewrap start and completion, users notified. Please capture audit log events: vault audit path, aws:kms CloudTrail entries, s3:GetObject events.
eve: I've redacted the leaked file content and uploaded a sanitized copy to the incident channel for reviewers. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/1766001234 (internal only).
alice: Confirming we need to rotate any long-lived service tokens that may have been signed using the wrapped keys. I'll run a search across repos for references to the old key id and kick owners to rotate.
bob: Estimated time: generate key + IAM + alias 10-20 mins; run rewrap for 120 wrapped objects ~ 30-45 mins; validate via vault audit events and spot-check decryption: another 15 mins. Total ~1.5 hours.
carol: If rewrap fails for any object, fallback plan: create new transit keys in Vault and re-encrypt at application layer, then update references.
dinesh: Pushed terraform branch and created PR #789. Tagging @alice for review on IAM principal list. PR link: https://git.internal/repo/infra/kms/pull/789
alice: Reviewing PR now.
sec-oncall: Communication: notify product security + legal (brief) and infra leadership. Prepare an internal postmortem template pinned to incident channel after containment.
eve: Any reason not to rotate the KMS CMK for production too? Might be overkill. Thoughts?
carol: Production CMKs are separate; no evidence of cross-account exposure. For now, scope to staging/backups only. If logs show cross-use, escalate to rotate prod keys.
alice: Post-action tasks: update backup retention policy + add lifecycle policy to deny storing vault-wrapped files unencrypted at rest beyond 30 days in staging; add S3 bucket policy requiring server-side encryption with our CMK and block public ACLs.
sec-oncall: Who will file the postmortem? bob?
bob: I'll draft the postmortem. Will include timeline, root cause (ACL drift), remediation steps, and follow-ups. Ping me with any missing artifacts.
infra-bot: audit_note: vault-audit.log appended -> s3://incidents/1766001234/audit.log (sha256: abc123...) :page_facing_up:
dinesh: IAM policy updated in PR. Also added a CloudTrail filter to emit alerts for kms:Decrypt calls from unusual principals. See PR comments.
alice: Token revoke confirmed, CI jobs using revoked token queued fail; creating replacement via github app token flow and updating required pipelines.
sec-oncall: Closing steps: 1) confirm rewrap completed, 2) verify no access to quarantined file, 3) postmortem + CSAT. Last_message_ts set to now.
eve: Thanks everyone. Greatly appreciate the quick coordination. :heart:
sec-oncall: Incident closed to monitoring state; if new findings surface re-open thread. :lock:
